key_insight: A hybrid SCAPS-1D + machine learning workflow can rapidly screen multilayer perovskite solar cells and identify high-efficiency, lead-free architectures without exhaustively simulating every material combination.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical design rulebook for optimizing ETL, absorber, and HTL choices to improve charge extraction and suppress recombination in next-generation perovskite solar cells.
method: Simulated 125 ETL/absorber/HTL device stacks with SCAPS-1D.
Trained an ML model on a subset to predict PCE for unseen structures.
Used SHAP to rank the most influential descriptors and guide physical interpretation.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed reliable ranking performance, and the top ML-suggested devices were confirmed by full SCAPS-1D simulations, including a best-case PCE of 28.85%.
watch_item: Model recommendations depend on the quality and coverage of the simulated training set, so performance may not transfer directly to materials or interfaces outside the explored design space.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
